title: Frobenius coherence for pullback, tensor and the ordinary adjunction
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For every finite-type $k_0$-scheme $W_0$ occurring below put $W=W_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g_W=\operatorname{id}_{W_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ with geometric Frobenius, and $P_W=Lg_W^*$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use the rational/common-stage bounded constructible categories and Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:P_WK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$, with morphisms $u\theta_K=\theta_LP_W(u)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Give the underlying operations their standard lifts: $H(K,\theta)=(HK,H(\theta)c_{H,K})$, where $c_H:P_{\rm out}H\xrightarrow{\sim}HP_{\rm in}$ is the canonical Frobenius comparison; tensor has structure $(\theta_M\otimes\theta_N)\mu_g$, and internal Hom has structure $R\mathcal Hom(\theta_M^{-1},\theta_N)h_g$. All assertions are restricted to full domains closed under the displayed composites where these operations and comparisons have the stated constructible typing. Retain all underlying finite-Tor, lattice-presentation and witnessed-origin restrictions. No separatedness of the structural morphisms $W_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is imposed.

Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ and $h_0:Y_0\to Z_0$ be separated finite-type morphisms, and write $f,h$ for their geometric base changes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the canonical pullback composition and tensor comparisons of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition, lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], rationalized and passed to common coefficient stages by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The composition comparison $L(hf)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*Lh^*$, the comparisons $Lf^*(M\otimes^LN)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*M\otimes^LLf^*N$, and tensor associativity, signed symmetry and unit comparisons are morphisms of Weil pairs. More precisely, for any such comparison $d:H\to J$, its specified Frobenius comparisons satisfy
$$d_{P_{\rm in}K}c_{H,K}=c_{J,K}P_{\rm out}(d_K),$$
with the corresponding multi-variable equation for tensor.

Use only the ordinary adjunction $L=Lf^*\dashv R=Rf_*$ of [fix-prop-adjunctions](1). Put $s:P_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}LP_Y$ for pullback composition in $fg_X=g_Yf$. The unit--square--counit formula for $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ [def-exchange-projection] is the right mate of $s^{-1}:LP_Y\to P_XL$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For the standard lifts of $L,R$, the unit $\eta_K:K\to RLK$ and counit $\varepsilon_M:LRM\to M$ satisfy
$$\theta_{RLK}P_Y(\eta_K)=\eta_K\theta_K,\qquad \varepsilon_M\theta_{LRM}=\theta_MP_X(\varepsilon_M).$$
These are the original ordinary unit and counit, and their triangle equations give the adjunction on Weil pairs. This does not require an exceptional adjoint.

proof.text:
Write $A_u=Lu^*$ and $G_W=P_W$, using ordinary composition of functors and reading products of arrows right to left. Write $c_{u,v}:A_{vu}\to A_uA_v$ for the specified pullback comparison. The Frobenius identity $fg_X=g_Yf$ gives precisely
$$s_f=c_{f,g_Y}c_{g_X,f}^{-1}:G_XA_f\longrightarrow A_fG_Y.$$
The semilinear field-operation lemma supplies the standard lifted functors on the stipulated domains, with this comparison for pullback and the specified comparison for direct image; it also supplies the equivalences $G_W$. In particular the Frobenius comparison for the composite functor $A_fA_h$ is $(A_f s_h)(s_f A_h)$. This is the structure obtained by applying the two lifts successively, since naturality of $s_f$ moves $A_h(\theta)$ past $s_f$.

proof.text: Use the associativity identity for $c$ first over $\mathcal O_E$. Rationalization sends it to the same identity over $E$: by the definition of the rational operations, both composites are the images of the integral composites. Naturality extends to every rational arrow by linearity on the localized Hom modules. For $E\subset L$, clause (1) of the pullback-identities scalar-extension lemma identifies the transported $c_E$ with $c_L$ after conjugation by the operation comparisons. Therefore the rational composition comparisons define the specified common-stage comparisons; their associativity equations agree after passing to a common field. These arguments concern the natural transformations and all their arrows, so do not require a Weil isomorphism to preserve an integral lattice. The tensor-comparison lemma already asserts its coherence and scalar-extension identities at all these coefficient stages.

proof.text:
For $f:X\to Y$, $h:Y\to Z$, put $d=c_{f,h}$. The composition comparison satisfies the required Frobenius equation
$$d_{G_ZK}s_{hf,K}=A_f(s_{h,K})s_{f,A_hK}G_X(d_K).$$
Here is the cancellation giving the equation. The associativity identity for $c$ on $(g_X,f,h)$ rewrites
$G_X(d)c_{g_X,hf}$ as $(c_{g_X,f}A_h)c_{fg_X,h}$.
On $(f,g_Y,h)$ it rewrites
$(c_{f,g_Y}A_h)c_{g_Yf,h}$ as $(A_fc_{g_Y,h})c_{f,hg_Y}$.
On $(f,h,g_Z)$ it rewrites
$(A_fc_{h,g_Z})c_{f,g_Zh}$ as $(dG_Z)c_{hf,g_Z}$.
Substitute $s_f=c_{f,g_Y}c_{g_X,f}^{-1}$ and $s_h=c_{h,g_Z}c_{g_Y,h}^{-1}$ into the right side, precompose with $c_{g_X,hf}$, and use these three identities in order. The adjacent inverse factors cancel and the result is $(dG_Z)c_{hf,g_Z}$. Since $c_{g_X,hf}$ is invertible, this is exactly the displayed equation. Step 2 gives the same computation at either field coefficient stage.

proof.text:
For tensor write $t_u=\mu_u$. The tensor/composition identity of the tensor-comparison lemma reads
$$t_{u;A_vM,A_vN}A_u(t_{v;M,N})c_{u,v;M\otimes N}=(c_{u,v;M}\otimes c_{u,v;N})t_{vu;M,N}.$$
Apply it to $(u,v)=(g_X,f)$ and $(f,g_Y)$. The two composite scheme maps are equal, so their $t_{vu}$ are the same. Solve the first identity for that common tensor comparison and substitute in the second. With $s_f=c_{f,g_Y}c_{g_X,f}^{-1}$, cancellation gives
$$t_{f;G_YM,G_YN}A_f(t_{g_Y;M,N})s_{f;M\otimes N}=(s_{f;M}\otimes s_{f;N})t_{g_X;A_fM,A_fN}G_X(t_{f;M,N}).$$
The comparison on the left before $t_f$ is the Frobenius comparison for $A_f(M\otimes N)$; the comparison on the right after $G_X(t_f)$ is that for $A_fM\otimes A_fN$. Thus this is the specified two-variable $d_Pc_H=c_JP(d)$ equation, rather than just an isomorphism between its endpoints.

proof.text:
Apply the associativity, signed symmetry and unit compatibility of $t_g$ in the tensor-comparison lemma. For example its symmetry equation is
$$\sigma_{GM,GN}t_{g;M,N}=t_{g;N,M}G(\sigma_{M,N}).$$
Its associativity equation is
$$\alpha_{GM,GN,GT}(t_{g;M,N}\otimes1)t_{g;M\otimes N,T}=(1\otimes t_{g;N,T})t_{g;M,N\otimes T}G(\alpha_{M,N,T}).$$
For the canonical unit comparison $e_g:G\mathbf1\to\mathbf1$, its left-unit equation is
$$\lambda_{GM}(e_g\otimes1)t_{g;\mathbf1,M}=G(\lambda_M),$$
and the right-unit equation is $\rho_{GM}(1\otimes e_g)t_{g;M,\mathbf1}=G(\rho_M)$. These are exactly the multi-variable Frobenius comparison equations for the tensor associator, symmetry and unitors (the unit object has Weil map $e_g$). The symmetry is the signed derived symmetry, not the unsigned symmetry on terms. All equations are available at the stipulated field stages by that lemma.

proof.text:
For a natural comparison $d:H\to J$ and a Weil object $(K,\theta)$, naturality and the comparison equation give
$$d_KH(\theta)c_{H,K}=J(\theta)d_{PK}c_{H,K}=J(\theta)c_{J,K}P(d_K).$$
By the definition of the morphisms of Weil pairs, this says exactly that $d_K$ is a Weil morphism. The same calculation uses naturality in each variable for tensor and its associator, symmetry and unitors. Apply it to the comparison equations proved in Steps 3--5. If $d_K$ is invertible, multiply its Weil equation by $d_K^{-1}$ and $P(d_K^{-1})$ to obtain the Weil equation for its inverse. Hence all the displayed isomorphisms are isomorphisms of Weil pairs. This calculation uses arbitrary rational/common-stage Weil maps, including ones not coming from a stable integral lattice.

proof.text:
Take $L=A_f$ and $R=Rf_*$ with the ordinary adjunction of fix-prop-adjunctions (1). In the Frobenius square the pullback-square map in the exchange definition is $s_f^{-1}:LP_Y\to P_XL$. Substituting it in the unit--square--counit definition gives
$$b_M=R(P_X\varepsilon_M)R(s_{f,RM}^{-1})\eta_{P_YRM}:P_YRM\longrightarrow RP_XM.$$
This is term for term the right-mate formula for $s_f^{-1}$, so $b=\operatorname{Ex}_*$ with the specified normalization. Its invertibility and the standard direct-image lift on these field domains are supplied by the semilinear field-operation lemma. Thus $\theta_{LK}=L(\theta_K)s_{f,K}$ and $\theta_{RM}=R(\theta_M)b_M$ are the very lifts in the item. The semilinear Frobenius square is used as a square of schemes (or with the source structural maps retagged); no $k$-linearity of $g_W$, or separatedness of $W_0$ over $k_0$, enters this formula.

proof.text:
Apply the fixed-pair adjunction-lift lemma with $\mathcal C=D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, $\mathcal D=D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ on the stipulated full domains, $F=P_Y$, $G=P_X$, and with its $e=s_f$ and $b=\operatorname{Ex}_*$. In that lemma's diagrammatic notation $LG$ means $G\circ L$, so its $e$ has exactly source $P_XL$ and target $LP_Y$. Step 7 verifies its mate hypothesis, and both comparison maps are isomorphisms. The lemma therefore identifies the lifted unit and counit with the carrier maps $\eta_K$ and $\varepsilon_M$. Writing out their fixed-pair morphism conditions gives precisely
$$R(L\theta_K\,s_{f,K})b_{LK}P_Y(\eta_K)=\eta_K\theta_K,$$
$$\varepsilon_M L(R\theta_M\,b_M)s_{f,RM}=\theta_MP_X(\varepsilon_M),$$
which are the two equations in the item after expanding $\theta_{RLK}$ and $\theta_{LRM}$. The domains are full and closed under these composites, so each component and each comparison in this application has the required constructible typing.

proof.text: The resulting unit and counit are natural because their carriers are the ordinary natural transformations and equality of fixed-pair arrows is equality of carriers. Their two triangle composites forget to $(R\varepsilon)(\eta R)$ and $(\varepsilon L)(L\eta)$, which are identities by the ordinary adjunction. Faithfulness of the forgetful functor therefore gives the same triangle equations for Weil pairs, establishing the claimed adjunction with these original maps. Every operation was restricted throughout to the full domains stipulated in the item; this proof enlarges neither those domains nor the class of morphisms for which an adjunction was supplied.
